status_summary: On 2026-01-21 HHS OCR issued a Notice of Violation to Illinois under the Weldon and Coats-Snowe Amendments over a state law tying conscience protections to abortion referral, and by a notice dated the same day disavowed an August 2021 letter that had withdrawn a 2020 Weldon violation finding against California, without reinstating that finding. On 2026-03-19 OCR announced Weldon investigations of thirteen unnamed states over requirements that health plans cover abortion. No withdrawal or disallowance of Medicaid or other HHS funds, and no DOJ litigation defending such a decision, was found; the 2020 disallowance of California Medicaid funds predates the period.

timeline.event: HHS OCR issued a Notice of Violation to Illinois finding a state law violates the Weldon and Coats-Snowe Amendments; the press release does not describe any funding consequence.

OCR notice (91 FR 3207, signed 2026-01-21, published 2026-01-26) disavows the legal positions in the August 2021 letter to the California Attorney General that had withdrawn OCR's January 2020 Notice of Violation under the Weldon Amendment; the notice does not reinstate the 2020 violation and describes no action on California's federal funds.

HHS OCR announced investigations of thirteen states under the Weldon Amendment over alleged pressure on health care entities to cover or pay for abortions, and said it had withdrawn the 2021 letter that excluded employers and plan sponsors from the law's protections; the release names no states and does not mention withholding funds, Medicaid or the Department of Justice.

OCR reorganization (91 FR 39626, published 2026-06-30, effective 2026-06-28) creates a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division that enforces conscience laws including the Weldon Amendment (Pub. L. 119-75, div. B, tit. V, sec. 507(d)); the notice describes no funding action.
